instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines who qualifies as a paid 'lobbyist' and prohibits anyone from engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed and authorized, effectively requiring paid lobbyists to be licensed/registered to lobby.
Lobbyist licenses expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year, implying renewal/registration at least every 24 months.
Lobbyists file a license application under §13.63 while principals separately file a registration statement under §13.64, indicating distinct filings by each party.
The lobbyist license application requirements include a social security number (or sworn statement of none) and signature, but no photograph requirement is stated.
Elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees are not subject to multiple lobbying provisions when acting in an official capacity.
Agencies that file a statement under §13.695 and named agency officials are expressly not subject to several key lobbying regulation sections, creating a partial exemption for government agencies.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text sets a 10-day change-notice rule for agencies (§13.695(2)) and a 10-day rule for principals to register after exceeding $500 (§13.64(1)), but it does not specify any deadline for lobbyists to notify the board of changes to their own license/registration information.

Wisconsin requires lobbyists to be licensed before engaging in lobbying (§13.66), but the statute does not provide a numeric 'days after first lobbying' deadline for the lobbyist to register; it is a precondition rather than a post-activity grace period.
